Name: 🤖 FreeTacMan
Description: FreeTacMan is a handheld gripper for manipulation data collection that carries visuo-tactile sensors on the fingerpads plus a wrist-mounted fisheye camera. The handheld gripper preserves natural fingertip motion and interaction. A universal gripper interface with quick-swap mounts lets the same end-effector attach to different arms.
Citation: Wu, Longyan, Checheng Yu, Jieji Ren, Li Chen, Yufei Jiang, Ran Huang, Guoying Gu, and Hongyang Li. "Freetacman: Robot-free visuo-tactile data collection system for contact-rich manipulation." 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) (2026).

Name: 🤖 Good Enough Manipulator (GEM)
Description: Good Enough Manipulator (GEM) is a 7-DOF arm, with up to 1.2 kg payload and a 3D printed structure, intended for robotics researchers and hobbyists. The arm runs on the LeRobot control stack for motor calibration, teleop, camera capture and policy training. The arm features a QDD motor for the shoulder, lower-cost and lighter Feetech servos for the rest of the joints, and the PincOpen gripper. A separate ~$120 leader arm is also released for teleoperated data collection.
Citation: N/A

Name: 🤖 reBot-DevArm
Description: reBot-DevArm (reBot Arm B601 DM/RS) is a 6-DOF desktop robot arm with ~1.5 kg payload and 650 mm reach. The arm is released in 2 variants: B601-DM (Damiao motors) and B601-RS (Robstride motors), and is built with sheet metal and 3D printed parts. A detailed BOM with links and assembly video are provided - and the project is OSHW certified (CN000024). Software stack supports Python sdk, ROS1/2, Pinocchio, IsaacSim, and LeRobot. The arm is compatible with an optional leader arm (Star Arm 102).
Citation: N/A

Name: 🤖 ShapeForce
Description: ShapeForce is a soft robotic wrist that deforms under contact interactions and provide force-like signals via marker-based pose tracking from a wrist-mounted RGB camera. The compliant core of the wrist is printed with TPU with rigid PLA connectors on either end. The cost of printed materials is <$10 (excluding the camera required for pose tracking).
Citation: Zhu, Jinxuan, Zihao Yan, Yangyu Xiao, Jingxiang Guo, Chenrui Tie, Xinyi Cao, Yuhang Zheng, and Lin Shao. "ShapeForce: Low-Cost Soft Robotic Wrist for Contact-Rich Manipulation." 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) (2026).

Name: 🤖 YUBI
Description: YUBI is finger-aligned handheld gripper for bimanual manipulation data-collection. The thumb and index/middle fingers drive the two jaws via internal gears so the gripper follows the operator's natural hand pinching motion, aimed at improving haptic transparency over UMI-style grippers. The gripper can also mount as an end-effector on different robot arms.
Citation: Ohkawa, Takehiko, Jumpei Arima, Yuki Noguchi, Masatoshi Tateno, Makoto Sugiura, Takuya Okubo, Kengo Ikeuchi et al. "YUBI: Yielding Universal Bidigital Interface for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation at Scale." arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.10244 (2026).

Name: 9DTact
Description: 9DTact is a compact, vision-based tactile sensor for 3D shape reconstruction and 6D force estimation. It leverages the reflective properties of silicone -- 2 different layers of silicone gel are stakced and an LED and camera are placed below. When an object contacts the gel surface, the translucent gel becomes thinner under pressure, reducing light reflection in these areas, which appear darker in the image. It means that the deeper you press, the darker you will see.
Citation: Lin, Changyi, Han Zhang, Jikai Xu, Lei Wu, and Huazhe Xu. "9dtact: A compact vision-based tactile sensor for accurate 3d shape reconstruction and generalizable 6d force estimation." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 9, no. 2 (2023): 923-930.

Name: Aero Hand Open
Description: Aero Hand Open from TetherIA is a 7 Active DOF (16 joints), tendon-driven anthropomorphic hand with open-source CAD, electronics, firmware, sdk, and ROS2 packages. The hand can also be purchased in both left and right versions either assembled ($600) or as an assembly kit ($314).
Citation: N/A

Name: AirExo-2
Description: AirExo-2 is a low-cost exoskeleton system for large-scale in-the-wild data collection, along with several adaptors that transform collected data into pseudo-robot demonstrations suitable for policy learning. AirExo-2 is designed to have a 1:1 scale and maintain kinematic isomorphism with the robotic arm. A mobile base is added to support data collection in diverse environments, and a dedicated calibration process is introduced to ensure accurate motion capture.
Citation: Fang, Hongjie, Chenxi Wang, Yiming Wang, Jingjing Chen, Shangning Xia, Jun Lv, Zihao He et al. "AirExo-2: Scaling up Generalizable Robotic Imitation Learning with Low-Cost Exoskeletons." Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) (2025).

Name: ALOHA
Description: ALOHA is a low-cost system that performs end-to-end imitation learning directly from real demonstrations, collected with a custom teleoperation interface.
Citation: Zhao, Tony, Vikash Kumar, Sergey Levine, and Chelsea Finn. "Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware." In Proceedings of the Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2023 Conference (2023).

Name: ALOHA 2
Description: ALOHA 2 is an enhanced version of ALOHA that has greater performance, ergonomics, and robustness compared to the original design.
Citation: Aldaco, Jorge, Travis Armstrong, Robert Baruch, Jeff Bingham, Sanky Chan, Kenneth Draper, Debidatta Dwibedi et al. "Aloha 2: An enhanced low-cost hardware for bimanual teleoperation." arXiv preprint arXiv:2405.02292 (2024).

Name: Amazing Hand
Description: Amazing Hand is an 8-dof humanoid hand with 4 fingers from Pollen Robotics. Each finger has 2 phalanxes articulated together with flexible shells allmost everywhere. All actuators are inside the hand, without any cables. The whole hand is 3D printable and has a 400g weight. The hand design is based on a simplified version of the ILDA Hand.
Citation: N/A

Name: AnySkin
Description: AnySkin is a skin sensor made for robotic touch that is easy to assemble, compatible with different robot end-effectors and generalizes to new skin instances. It is built on the simplistic design of ReSkin, and decoupling the sensing electronics from the sensing interface. AnySkin senses contact through distortions in magnetic field generated by magnetized iron particles in the sensing surface. The flexible surface is physically separated from its electronics, which allows for easy replacability when damaged.
Citation: Bhirangi, Raunaq, Venkatesh Pattabiraman, Enes Erciyes, Yifeng Cao, Tess Hellebrekers, and Lerrel Pinto. "Anyskin: Plug-and-play skin sensing for robotic touch." In 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), pp. 16563-16570. IEEE, 2025.

Name: ARMADA
Description: ARMADA (Affordable Robot for Manipulation and Dynamic Actions) is a 6 degrees-of-freedom bimanual robot designed for dynamic manipulation research. ARMADA combines low-inertia, back-drivable actuators with a lightweight design, using readily available components and 3D-printed links for ease of assembly in research labs.
Citation: Kim, Jaehyung, Jiho Kim, Dongryung Lee, Yujin Jang, and Beomjoon Kim. "A low-cost and lightweight 6 DoF bimanual arm for dynamic and contact-rich manipulation." Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) (2025).

Name: Berkeley Humanoid Lite
Description: Berkeley Humanoid Lite is an open-source humanoid robot with a modular 3D-printed gearbox for the actuators and robot body. All components can be sourced from widely available e-commerce platforms and fabricated using standard desktop 3D printers, keeping the total hardware cost under $5,000
Citation: Chi, Yufeng, Qiayuan Liao, Junfeng Long, Xiaoyu Huang, Sophia Shao, Borivoje Nikolic, Zhongyu Li, and Koushil Sreenath. "Demonstrating Berkeley Humanoid Lite: An Open-source, Accessible, and Customizable 3D-printed Humanoid Robot."Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) (2025).

Name: CoinFT
Description: CoinFT, a capacitive 6-axis force/torque (F/T) sensor that is compact, light, low-cost, and robust with an average mean-squared error of 0.11N for force and 0.84mNm for moment when the input ranges from 0~10N and 0~4N in normal and shear directions, respectively. CoinFT is a stack of two rigid PCBs with comb-shaped electrodes connected by an array of silicone rubber pillars. The microcontroller interrogates the electrodes in different subsets in order to enhance sensitivity for measuring 6-axis F/T.
Citation: Choi, Hojung, Jun En Low, Tae Myung Huh, Gabriela A. Uribe, Seongheon Hong, Kenneth AW Hoffman, Julia Di, Tony G. Chen, Andrew A. Stanley, and Mark R. Cutkosky. "CoinFT: A Coin-Sized, Capacitive 6-Axis Force Torque Sensor for Robotic Applications." arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.19225 (2025).

Name: Controller for Humanoid Imitation and Live Demonstration (CHILD)
Description: Controller for Humanoid Imitation and Live Demonstration (CHILD) is a compact reconfigurable teleoperation system that enables joint level control over humanoid robots. CHILD fits within a standard baby carrier, allowing the operator control over all four limbs, and supports both direct joint mapping for fullbody control and loco-manipulation. Adaptive force feedback is incorporated to enhance operator experience and prevent unsafe joint movements.
Citation: Myers, Noboru, Obin Kwon, Sankalp Yamsani, and Joohyung Kim. "CHILD (Controller for Humanoid Imitation and Live Demonstration): a Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation System." IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids) (2025).

Name: CRAFT Hand
Description: CRAFT Hand is a tendon-driven anthropomorphic hand with hybrid hard-soft compliance. It uses soft materials at joints and rigid materials for the links. The joints are rolling-contact surfaces to keep flexion on repeatable motion paths. The full design costs under $600 and uses 15 actuators.
Citation: Lin, Leo, Shivansh Patel, Jay Moon, Svetlana Lazebnik, and Unnat Jain. "CRAFT: A Tendon-Driven Hand with Hybrid Hard-Soft Compliance." arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.12120 (2026).

Name: DexUMI
Description: DexUMI is a framework with hardware and software adaptation components that is designed to minimize the action and observation gaps. The hardware adaptation takes the form of a wearable hand exoskeleton that a user can wear to directly collect manipulation data. The exoskeleton is designed for two different dexterous hand types: a 6-DoF Inspire hand and a 12-DoF XHand. Hardware optimization framework refines exoskeleton parameters (e.g., link lengths) to closely match the robot finger trajectories while maintaining wearability for the human hand.
Citation: Xu, Mengda, Han Zhang, Yifan Hou, Zhenjia Xu, Linxi Fan, Manuela Veloso, and Shuran Song. "DexUMI: Using Human Hand as the Universal Manipulation Interface for Dexterous Manipulation." Proceedings of The 9th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) (2025).

Name: DexWild-System
Description:
DexWild-System is a portable, high-fidelity, and embodiment-agnostic data collection system capable of efficiently gathering dexterous human hand data across many environments. It consists of three components: a single tracking camera for wrist pose estimation, a battery-powered mini-PC for onboard data capture, and a
custom sensor pod comprising a motion-capture glove and synchronized palm-mounted cameras.
Citation: Tao, Tony, Mohan Kumar Srirama, Jason Jingzhou Liu, Kenneth Shaw, and Deepak Pathak. "Dexwild: Dexterous human interactions for in-the-wild robot policies." Robotics: Science & Systems (RSS) (2025).

Name: Digit
Description: An inexpensive, compact, and high-resolution tactile sensor geared towards in-hand manipulation. Digit improves upon past vision-based tactile sensors by miniaturizing the form factor to be mountable on multi-fingered hands, and by providing several design improvements that result in an easier, more repeatable manufacturing process, and enhanced reliability. Equipped with over 18 unique sensing features, Digit 360 allows researchers to either combine its various sensing technologies or isolate individual signals for in-depth analysis of each modality.
Citation:
Lambeta, Mike, Po-Wei Chou, Stephen Tian, Brian Yang, Benjamin Maloon, Victoria Rose Most, Dave Stroud et al. "Digit: A novel design for a low-cost compact high-resolution tactile sensor with application to in-hand manipulation." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 5, no. 3 (2020): 3838-3845.

Lambeta, Mike, Tingfan Wu, Ali Sengul, Victoria Rose Most, Nolan Black, Kevin Sawyer, Romeo Mercado et al. "Digitizing touch with an artificial multimodal fingertip." arXiv preprint arXiv:2411.02479 (2024).

Name: DigiTac
Description: DigiTac is a customized version of the DIGIT high-resolution tactile sensor (from Facebook AI Research and GelSight) to have a 3D-printed sensing surface based on the TacTip family of soft biomimetic optical tactile sensors. The DIGIT-TacTip (DigiTac) enables direct comparison between these distinct tactile sensor types.
Citation: Lepora, Nathan F., Yijiong Lin, Ben Money-Coomes, and John Lloyd. "DigiTac: A DIGIT-TacTip hybrid tactile sensor for comparing low-cost high-resolution robot touch." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 7, no. 4 (2022): 9382-9388.

Name: DOGlove
Description: DOGlove is a low-cost, precise, and haptic force feedback glove system for teleoperation and manipulation. It features a customized joint structure for 21-DoF motion capture, a compact cable-driven torque transmission mechanism for 5-DoF multidirectional force feedback, and a linear resonate actuator for 5-DoF fingertip haptic feedback.
Citation: Zhang, Han, Songbo Hu, Zhecheng Yuan, and Huazhe Xu. "Doglove: Dexterous manipulation with a low-cost open-source haptic force feedback glove." Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) (2025).

Name: EN02-OP
Description: Open Source 3-Finger End-Effector created by Westwood Robotics. A very simple yet versital 7DoF design, enabling the end-effector to change into the best poses for all kinds of items.
Citation: N/A

Name: FastUMI
Description: FastUMI is a redesign of the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) system that enables rapid deployment, simplifies hardware-software integration, and delivers robust performance in real-world data acquisition. It removes dependencies on specialized robotic components, ensures visual consistency between handheld and robot-mounted configurations, and reduces reliance on external computational framework.
Citation: Liu, Kehui, Chuyue Guan, Zhongjie Jia, Ziniu Wu, Xin Liu, Tianyu Wang, Shuai Liang et al. "FastUMI: A Scalable and Hardware-Independent Universal Manipulation Interface with Dataset." arXiv preprint arXiv:2409.19499 (2025).

Name: GELLO
Description: GELLO is a framework for building low-cost teleoperation devices for collecting robot demonstrations. A GELLO is scaled, kinematically equivalent leader arm of a target robot, built from 3D-printed parts and Dynamixel actuators. The builds for specific arms (Franka Panda/FR3, UR, xARM, and YAM) are released and can be easily extended to other robot arms.
Citation: Wu, Philipp, Yide Shentu, Zhongke Yi, Xingyu Lin, and Pieter Abbeel. "Gello: A general, low-cost, and intuitive teleoperation framework for robot manipulators." In 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), pp. 12156-12163. IEEE, 2024.

Name: GelSlim
Description: GelSlim 4.0 is a new open-source, vision-based tactile sensor designed to promote reproducibility and accessibility across research and hobbyist communities. Building upon the GelSlim 3.0 sensor, our design features two key improvements: a simplified, modifiable finger structure and easily manufacturable lenses. An open-source depth and shear field estimation algorithms are also provided to enable in-hand pose estimation, slip detection, and other manipulation tasks.
Citation: Taylor, Ian H., Siyuan Dong, and Alberto Rodriguez. "Gelslim 3.0: High-resolution measurement of shape, force and slip in a compact tactile-sensing finger." 2022 International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA). IEEE, 2022.

Name: Grasp EveryThing (GET)
Description: Grasp EveryThing (GET) gripper is a 1-DoF, 3-finger design for securely grasping objects of different shapes and sizes. Mounted on a standard parallel jaw actuator, the design features three narrow, tapered fingers arranged in a two-against-one configuration, where the two fingers converge into a V-shape. Tactile sensing can be integrated into the standalone finger via an externally-mounted camera.
Citation: Burgess, Michael, and Edward H. Adelson. "Grasp everything (get): 1-dof, 3-fingered gripper with tactile sensing for robust grasping." In 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), pp. 4714-4721. IEEE, 2025.

Name: Insight
Description: Insight is a soft thumb-sized vision-based haptic sensor that can enbable robots feel directional force distributions all over a 3D conical surface.  Constructed around an internal monocular camera, the sensor has only a single layer of elastomer over-moulded on a stiff frame to guarantee sensitivity, robustness and soft contact.
Citation: Sun, Huanbo, Katherine J. Kuchenbecker, and Georg Martius. "A soft thumb-sized vision-based sensor with accurate all-round force perception." Nature Machine Intelligence 4, no. 2 (2022): 135-145.

Name: ISyHand
Description: ISyHand (pronounced easy-hand) is a highly dexterous, low-cost, easy-to-manufacture, on-joint servo-driven robot hand. The hand uses off-the-shelf Dynamixel motors, fasteners, and 3D-printed parts, can be assembled within four hours, and has a total material cost of about 1,300 USD. The ISyHand’s unique articulated-palm design increases overall dexterity with only a modest sacrifice in anthropomorphism.
Citation: Richardson, Benjamin A., Felix Grüninger, Lukas Mack, Joerg Stueckler, and Katherine J. Kuchenbecker. "ISyHand: A Dexterous Multi-finger Robot Hand with an Articulated Palm." IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids) (2025).

Name: K-Bot
Description:
K-Bot from K-Scale Labs is an open-source humanoid robot. The hardware of the robot is modular and customizable, and has an adaptable end effector design to equip the robot with one of their supported end effectors, or design your own for custom applications.

Although K-Scale is no longer sellling the K-bot, the open-sourced hardware and software files are still available on their website.
Citation: N/A

Name: Koch v1.1
Description: Koch v1.1 is a leader/follower robot arm system. It's an improved version of the original Rau Robotics/Alexander Koch's robot to ease assembly. With Hugging Face's LeRobot framework, it's simple to get the arm set up and running with today's most up to date an capable machine learning systems.
Citation: N/A

Name: LEAP Hand
Description: LEAP Hand is a low-cost dexterous and anthropomorphic hand for machine learning research. In contrast to previous hands, LEAP Hand has a novel kinematic structure that allows maximal dexterity regardless of finger pose. LEAP Hand is low-cost and can be assembled in 4 hours at a cost of 2000 USD from readily available parts. It is capable of consistently exerting large torques over long durations of time.
Citation: Shaw, Kenneth, Ananye Agarwal, and Deepak Pathak. "Leap hand: Low-cost, efficient, and anthropomorphic hand for robot learning." Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) (2023).

Name: LEGATO Gripper
Description: LEGATO is a handheld gripper that unifies action and observation spaces, allowing tasks to be defined consistently across robots. Its modular and open source design aims to advance cross-embodiment robot learning research. Gripper motions generated by the policies are retargeted into high-degree-of-freedom whole-body motions using inverse kinematics for deployment across diverse embodiments.
Citation: Seo, Mingyo, H. Andy Park, Shenli Yuan, Yuke Zhu, and Luis Sentis. "Legato: Cross-embodiment imitation using a grasping tool." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (2025).

Name: MagiClaw
Description: MagiClaw is a versatile two-finger end-effector that can be hand-held by human operators or mounted on a robotic arm. It captures comprehensive action data (including kinematic motion, force, and contact deformation) from real-world demonstrations. The fingers feature soft, parallel-mechanism-driven designs, each with a miniature camera for vision-based deformable perception. An iPhone (with integrated LiDAR) provides additional environmental sensing and processes all sensor streams via a custom iOS application.
Citation: Wu, Tianyu, Xudong Han, Haoran Sun, Zishang Zhang, Bangchao Huang, Chaoyang Song, and Fang Wan. "MagiClaw: A Dual-Use, Vision-Based Soft Gripper for Bridging the Human Demonstration to Robotic Deployment Gap." In Workshop on Making Sense of Data in Robotics: Composition, Curation, and Interpretability at Scale at CoRL 2025.

Name: Magpie Gripper
Description: Magpie gripper is a low-cost gripper with individually actuated 4-bar linkages. The fingers have torque sensing at the actuators via current control, and the gripper has an RGB-D camera in the palm.
Citation: Correll, Nikolaus, Dylan Kriegman, Stephen Otto, and James Watson. "A versatile robotic hand with 3D perception, force sensing for autonomous manipulation." arXiv preprint arXiv:2402.06018 (2024).

Name: Midas Hand
Description: Midas Hand is a 4-fingered 16 DOF (13 active) anthropomorphic hand built with 13 Dynamixel XM335-T323-T actuators located at the joints and 3-axis tactile sensors on the fingertips. The release includes CAD files, BOM and assembly files, as well as MuJoCo model and software for control, retargeting, and teleop.
Citation: Zhu, Alvin, Mingzhang Zhu, Beom Jun Kim, Quanyou Wang, Jose Victor SH Ramos, and Dennis Hong. "MIDAS Hand: Modular low-Impedance Direct-drive Anthropomorphic Sensing Hand." arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.14487 (2026).

Name: Minsight
Description: Minsight is the miniaturized version of the vision-based tactile sensor Insight. It is roughly the size of a human fingertip and can sense directional force distributions all over a 3D sensing surface at 60 Hz. Constructed around an internal monocular camera, the sensor has only a single layer of elastomer over-moulded on a stiff frame to guarantee sensitivity, robustness and soft contact.
Citation: Andrussow, Iris, Huanbo Sun, Katherine J. Kuchenbecker, and Georg Martius. "Minsight: A Fingertip‐Sized Vision‐Based Tactile Sensor for Robotic Manipulation." Advanced Intelligent Systems 5, no. 8 (2023): 2300042.

Name: Mobile ALOHA
Description: Mobile ALOHA, a low-cost and whole-body teleoperation system for data collection, augments the ALOHA system with a mobile base, and a whole-body teleoperation interface.
Citation: Fu, Zipeng, Tony Z. Zhao, and Chelsea Finn. "Mobile aloha: Learning bimanual mobile manipulation with low-cost whole-body teleoperation." In Proceedings of the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2024 (2024).

Name: OpenArm
Description: OpenArm is an open-source 7DOF humanoid arm designed for physical AI research and deployment in contact-rich environments. All hardware and software are completely open-source and ready for you to build, hack, and deploy. OpenArm is designed with human-like proportions and dimensions, and built with QDD backdrivable motors and high compliance. Every component is designed to be purchasable and buildable.
Citation: N/A

Name: OpenHand
Description: The Yale OpenHand Project is an initiative to advance the design and use of robotic hands designed and built through rapid-prototyping techniques in order to encourage more variation and innovation in mechanical hardware. This project intends to establish a series of open-source hand designs, and through the contributions of the open-source user community, result in a large number of useful design modifications and variations available to researchers.
Citation: Ma, Raymond, and Aaron Dollar. "Yale openhand project: Optimizing open-source hand designs for ease of fabrication and adoption." IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine 24.1 (2017): 32-40.

Name: ORCA Hand
Description: The ORCA hand is a 17-DoF tendon-driven robotic hand with fully integrated tactile sensors that can be assembled in under 8 hours and has a BOM of $2k. We showcase design features such as popping joints, auto-calibration, and tensioning systems that significantly reduce complexity while increasing reliability, accuracy, and robustness.
Citation: Christoph, Clemens C., Maximilian Eberlein, Filippos Katsimalis, Arturo Roberti, Aristotelis Sympetheros, Michel R. Vogt, Davide Liconti et al. "ORCA: An Open-Source, Reliable, Cost-Effective, Anthropomorphic Robotic Hand for Uninterrupted Dexterous Task Learning." arXiv preprint arXiv:2504.04259 (2025).

Name: PAROL6 Robotic Arm
Description: PAROL6 is a high-performance 3D-printed desktop robotic arm. The design approach of PAROL6 was to be similar to industrial robots in terms of mechanical design, control software, and usability. Control software, GUI, and robots STL files are open-source.
Citation: N/A

Name: PincOpen
Description: Pinc’Open is a low-cost (~25€) and open-source parallel-finger gripper, derived from Pollen Robotics Reachy 2’s gripper. The gripper is also compatible with the SO-ARM100 open-source arm. And the fingertip on the gripper is interchangeable.
Citation: N/A

Name: Punyo
Description: Punyo soft-bubble gripper system combines highly compliant gripping surfaces with dense-geometry visuotactile sensing and facilitates multiple kinds of tactile perception. We first present several mechanical design advances on the Soft-bubble sensors including a fabrication technique to deposit custom patterns to the internal surface of the sensor membrane that enables tracking of shear-induced displacement of the grasped object. The depth maps output by the internal imaging sensor are used in an in-hand proximity pose estimation framework.
Citation: Kuppuswamy, Naveen, Alex Alspach, Avinash Uttamchandani, Sam Creasey, Takuya Ikeda, and Russ Tedrake. "Soft-bubble grippers for robust and perceptive manipulation. In 2020 IEEE." In RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), pp. 9917-9924.

Name: R-Tac Sensor
Description: R-Tac is a omnidirectional fingertip vision-based tactile sensor developed for "PP-Tac: Paper Picking Using Tactile Feedback in Dexterous Robotic Hands." R-Tac is a spherical tactile sensor designed with ease of fabrication, calibration, and scalable deployment. It can be integrated into each fingertip of a fully actuated dexterous robotic hand, enabling real-time contact feedback during manipulation tasks.
Citation: Lin, Pei, Yuzhe Huang, Wanlin Li, Jianpeng Ma, Chenxi Xiao, and Ziyuan Jiao. "PP-Tac: Paper Picking Using Tactile Feedback in Dexterous Robotic Hands." Robotics: Science and Systems(RSS) (2025).

Name: Reachy 2
Description: Reachy 2 is an open-source humanoid robot specifically designed for the development of embodied AI and real-world applications. Reachy 2 is fully open source, can be teleoperated or controlled with Python, and runs on ROS2 Foxy.  Its 3D-printed structure and off-the-shelf actuators make it inexpensive relatively to the price of an industrial-grade robot. Using an open-source architecture, its design makes it broadly connectable and customizable, so it can be integrated into many applications. Reachy is developed in partnership with and distributed by Pollen Robotics.
Citation: Mick, Sébastien, Mattieu Lapeyre, Pierre Rouanet, Christophe Halgand, Jenny Benois-Pineau, Florent Paclet, Daniel Cattaert, Pierre-Yves Oudeyer, and Aymar de Rugy. "Reachy, a 3D-printed human-like robotic arm as a testbed for human-robot control strategies." Frontiers in neurorobotics 13 (2019).

Name: Rebelia Hand
Description: Rebelia Hand project is an open-source, humanlike robotic hand designed for researchers, students, and robotics enthusiasts. The goal is to provide an affordable, high-performance robotic hand under 2000 EUR, open to community contributions and continuous improvement. This project hardware is released under the CERN Open Hardware License (OHL-S), ensuring the design remains open-source and preventing patent claims on its core innovations. The firmware is released under the GNU-GPL License. The documentation is released under the CC-BY-SA License.
Citation: N/A

Name: ReSkin
Description: ReSkin is a tactile soft sensor that leverages machine learning and magnetic sensing to offer a low-cost, diverse and compact solution for long-term use. Magnetic sensing separates the electronic circuitry from the passive interface, making it easier to replace interfaces as they wear out while allowing for a wide variety of form factors. Machine learning allows us to learn sensor response models that are robust to variations across fabrication and time, and our self-supervised learning algorithm enables finer performance enhancement with small, inexpensive data collection procedures.
Citation: Bhirangi, Raunaq, Tess Hellebrekers, Carmel Majidi, and Abhinav Gupta. "Reskin: versatile, replaceable, lasting tactile skins."Proceedings of CoRL (2021).

Name: Robot Nano Hand
Description: Robot Nano Hand is a 3D printed, tendon-driven anthropomorphic robot hand that is roughly human-sized. The hand uses 11 servos and also has palm-mounted Raspberry Pi V2 camera.
Citation: N/A

Name: RObotics BEnchmarks for Learning (ROBEL)
Description: ROBEL (RObotics BEnchmarks for Learning): a collection of affordable, reliable hardware designs for studying dexterous manipulation and locomotion on real-world hardware. With simple assembly instructions, detailed simulations, and all open-sourced software, we hope to open up the field of Reinforcement Learning to everyone and accelerate progress around the world.
Citation: Ahn, Michael, Henry Zhu, Kristian Hartikainen, Hugo Ponte, Abhishek Gupta, Sergey Levine, and Vikash Kumar. "Robel: Robotics benchmarks for learning with low-cost robots." In Conference on robot learning, pp. 1300-1313. PMLR, 2020.

Name: RUKA Hand
Description: RUKA is an open-source robot hand for researchers, hobbiests, and anyone who wants to build it! All parts are either 3D printed or off-the-shelf. Since RUKA is tendon-driven and has no joint encoders, fingertip and joint angle control is learned by putting a Manus motion capture glove onto RUKA and then mapping the position readings to the motor positions.
Citation: Zorin, Anya, Irmak Guzey, Billy Yan, Aadhithya Iyer, Lisa Kondrich, Nikhil X. Bhattasali and Lerrel Pinto. “RUKA: Rethinking the Design of Humanoid Hands with Learning.” Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS)(2025).

Name: RUKA-v2
Description: Ruka-v2 is a tendon-driven, anthropomorphic hand with 16 DOF across fingers and thumb plus 2 DOF parallel wrist. The hand has mostly 3D printed parts with off-the-shelf bearings, fasteners, and springs. Ruka-v2 also adds controlled abduction/adduction with passive spring return at the MCP joints of the fingers.
Citation: Liu, Xinqi Lucas, Ruoxi Hu, Alejandro Ojeda Olarte, Zhuoran Chen, Kenny Ma, Charles Cheng Ji, Lerrel Pinto, Raunaq Bhirangi, and Irmak Guzey. "Ruka-v2: Tendon Driven Open-Source Dexterous Hand with Wrist and Abduction for Robot Learning." arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.26660 (2026).

Name: SSG48 Adaptive Electric Gripper
Description: SSG-48 adaptive electric gripper is a gripper based on Spectral micro BLDC drivers. It is a gripper capable of controlling its gripping force, making it perfect for assembly tasks and human-robot collaboration. Force can be adjusted from 5 N to 80 N allowing you to grasp a wide range of items; from delicate and soft to rigid and sturdy. Mechanical files and firmware are open source allowing you to add a custom griping tool and attach it to any robotic arm or robot. Gripper software is also open-source. Gripper has a stroke of 48 mm and a mass of 400g.
Citation: N/A

Name: Standard Open Arm 100 (SO-100)
Description: Standard Open Arm 100 (SO-100) is a 3D printed follower and leader setup with arms for teleoperation setup that have the same off the shelf parts. The arm can be used with the LeRobot library from HuggingFace which aims to provide models, datasets, and tools for real-world robotics in PyTorch. LeRobot contains state-of-the-art approaches that have been shown to transfer to the real-world with a focus on imitation learning and reinforcement learning. LeRobot provides pretrained models, datasets with human collected demonstrations, and simulation environments.
Citation: Cadene, Remi, Simon Alibert, Alexander Soare, Quentin Gallouedec, Adil Zouitine, and Thomas Wolf. Lerobot: State-of-the-art machine learning for real-world robotics in pytorch. 2024.

Name: Tactile SoftHand-A
Description: Tactile SoftHand-A is a 3D-printed, highly-underactuated, tactile-sensorized, five-finger robotic hand inspired by the Pisa/IIT SoftHand. It features an antagonistic mechanism to actively open and close the hand, and the dual-tendon design allows active control of specific (distal or proximal interphalangeal) joints. The hand also integrates a new design of fully 3D-printed vision-based tactile sensor within the fingers that requires minimal hand assembly.
Citation: Li, Haoran, Christopher J. Ford, Chenghua Lu, Yijiong Lin, Matteo Bianchi, Manuel G. Catalano, Efi Psomopoulou, and Nathan F. Lepora. "Tactile SoftHand-A: 3D-printed, tactile, highly underactuated, anthropomorphic robot hand with an antagonistic tendon mechanism." The International Journal of Robotics Research (2024): 02783649251379516.

Name: TacTip
Description: TacTip is a 3d-printed optical tactile sensor that aims to fulfil the need for a cheap, robust, versatile tactile sensor, mountable on industrial robot arms and aimed at eventual integration into robot hands for manipulation. The sensor contacts objects with a compliant tip made from a moulded silicone rubber (Smooth-on Vytaflex 60) filled with a clear silicone gel (RTV27905). The inside of the tip comprises of a series of geometrically arranged white-tipped pins.
Citation: Chorley, Craig, Chris Melhuish, Tony Pipe, and Jonathan Rossiter. "Development of a tactile sensor based on biologically inspired edge encoding." In 2009 International Conference on Advanced Robotics, pp. 1-6. IEEE, 2009.

Name: TF-Gripper
Description: TF-Gripper is a low-cost (~$150) tactile parallel-jaw gripper designed for learning force-regulated robotic manipulation. It integrates a tactile sensing array on the fingertip and an external camera mounted on the wrist. The gripper is designed to be used for using force control when handling fragile or deformable objects. It has an effective force range of 0.45-45 N and is compatible with FR3 and UR5, and the adapter plate can be modified for other arms.
Citation: Kang, Xuhui, Tongxuan Tian, Sung-Wook Lee, Binghao Huang, Yunzhu Li, and Yen-Ling Kuo. "Learning Force-Regulated Manipulation with a Low-Cost Tactile-Force-Controlled Gripper." arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.10013 (2026).

Name: Thor Arm
Description: Thor is an Open Source and printable robot arm with 6 degrees of freedom. Its configuration (yaw-roll-roll-yaw-roll-yaw) is the same used by most of the manipulator robots on the market. In its extended position, Thor is about 625mm high and can lift loads up to 750 grams.
Citation: N/A

Name: TidyBot++
Description: TidyBot++ is an open-source design for an inexpensive, robust, and flexible mobile manipulator that can support arbitrary arms, enabling a wide range of real-world household mobile manipulation tasks. The design uses powered casters to enable the mobile base to be fully holonomic, able to control all planar degrees of freedom independently and simultaneously. This feature makes the base more maneuverable and simplifies many mobile manipulation tasks, eliminating the kinematic constraints that create complex and time-consuming motions in nonholonomic bases.
Citation: Wu, Jimmy, William Chong, Robert Holmberg, Aaditya Prasad, Yihuai Gao, Oussama Khatib, Shuran Song, Szymon Rusinkiewicz, and Jeannette Bohg. "TidyBot++: An Open-Source Holonomic Mobile Manipulator for Robot Learning." Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) (2024).

Name: ToddlerBot
Description: ToddlerBot is a low-cost, open-source humanoid robot platform designed for scalable policy learning and research in robotics and AI. ToddlerBot has 30 active DoFs (7 DoFs per arm, 6 DoFs per leg, a 2-DoF neck, and a 2-DoF waist)
Citation: Shi, Haochen, Weizhuo Wang, Shuran Song, and C. Karen Liu. "Toddlerbot: Open-source ml-compatible humanoid platform for loco-manipulation." arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.00893 (2025).

Name: TriFinger
Description: The TriFinger is a robotic platform intended to support research in dexterous manipulation. All hardware and software (including a simulator) are open-source. Each finger has 3 DoF and they share a workspace, permitting complex fine-manipulation. Three RGB cameras ensure good visibility for any configuration. Instructions for building your own platform can be found on the website.
Maintainer(s): Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
Citation: Wüthrich, Manuel, Felix Widmaier, Felix Grimminger, Joel Akpo, Shruti Joshi, Vaibhav Agrawal, Bilal Hammoud et al. "Trifinger: An open-source robot for learning dexterity." arXiv preprint arXiv:2008.03596 (2020).

Name: TRLC-DK1
Description: The DK1 from The Robot Learning Company is single-arm robot learning kit with leader and follower arms, and two cameras. The arms have a 700mm reach and 1kg payload. The hardware can be built from scratch using the open-source design and documentation, or purchased as a kit in single arm or bimanual configurations.
Citation: N/A

Name: Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) Gripper
Description: Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) -- a data collection and policy learning framework that allows direct skill transfer from in-the-wild human demonstrations to deployable robot policies. UMI employs hand-held grippers coupled with careful interface design to enable portable, low-cost, and information-rich data collection for challenging bimanual and dynamic manipulation demonstrations.
Citation: Chi, Cheng, Zhenjia Xu, Chuer Pan, Eric Cousineau, Benjamin Burchfiel, Siyuan Feng, Russ Tedrake, and Shuran Song. "Universal manipulation interface: In-the-wild robot teaching without in-the-wild robots." Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) (2024).

Name: Yeah Hand
Description: Yeah Hand (formerly Rebelia Hand) is an open source tendon-driven anthropomorphic robotic hand with 15 DOF and uses 5 Servomotors. The servo motors have torque feedback and can apply 25 Kg*cm per finger.
Citation: N/A

Name: Your Own Robot (YOR)
Description: YOR (Your Own Robot) is an open-source dual-arm mobile manipulator with a ~$10k BOM. YOR has an omnidirectional base, a telescopic vertical lift, and two arms (AgileX PiPER arms) with custom grippers. The footprint of the robot is 43×34.5 cm and the vertical lift has a stroke length of 63.5 cm. The robot also has a ZED 2i stereo camera onboard.
Citation: Anjaria, Manan H., Mehmet Enes Erciyes, Vedant Ghatnekar, Neha Navarkar, Haritheja Etukuru, Xiaole Jiang, Kanad Patel et al. "YOR: Your Own Mobile Manipulator for Generalizable Robotics." arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.11150 (2026).
